title: Water supply to be restored within next few hours
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) said the temporarily suspended water supply will be restored within the next few hours following the resolution of an emergency situation that affected water quality at the Kelani River water intake point.

title: Underworld figure ‘Bus Lalith’ brought from Dubai
byline: Underworld figure Lalith Kannangara, also known as ‘Bus Lalith’, who was arrested in Dubai, was brought to Sri Lanka this morning (25), Sri Lanka Police said.

title: Water supply temporarily suspended in Colombo and Gampaha areas
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has temporarily suspended the water supply to several areas in the Colombo and Gampaha districts due to an emergency situation that may affect the quality of water at the intake point of the Kelani River.

title: Indian nationals nabbed at BIA with cigarettes worth Rs. 834,000
byline: Two Indian nationals were arrested by officers of the Airport Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB) in the early hours of today (25) for allegedly attempting to illegally bring a consignment of Chinese-manufactured cigarettes worth approximately Rs. 834,000 into Sri Lanka and remove them from Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA).

title: Defence case concludes in Easter Sunday attacks trial; verdict set for September 22
byline: The defence case in the Easter Sunday terror attacks trial, in which 23,270 charges have been filed against 24 accused, including Mohamed Ibrahim Mohamed Naufar alias Naufar Moulavi, concluded yesterday.

title: Sri Lanka to launch oil, gas licensing round today
byline: Sri Lanka will launch today a new licensing round for offshore oil and gas exploration this year, with the Petroleum Development Authority of Sri Lanka (PDASL) preparing to invite international energy companies to explore and develop the country’s petroleum resources.

title: French tourist dies in Death Valley after car gets stuck in mud
byline: A French tourist has died in California’s Death Valley after becoming stranded on the side of the road during 46.6C (116F) heat.

title: India’s TCS to buy Porsche’s IT unit, bags 5-year deal worth $1.46 billion
byline: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS), will buy Porsche AG’s (P911_p.DE), automotive and consulting unit MHP, ​the IT major said on Monday, as part of ‌a wider partnership under which Porsche has committed €1.25 billion ($1.46 billion) for the Indian firm and MHP.

title: Iran vows to retaliate after US widens sanctions
byline: Iran promised to retaliate against expanded U.S. economic sanctions that the Americans said would cut off Iran’s economic ​lifeline, with Tehran expressing confidence that major trading partners would resist Washington’s pressure campaign.

title: Ranjith Rajasinghe assumes duties as new CAASL Chairman
byline: Ranjith Rajasinghe assumed duties today (25) as the new Chairman of the Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL), at the authority’s premises.

title: Police reveal charges against ‘Bus Lalith’ after Dubai repatriation
byline: Police today revealed the charges against Lalith Kannangara, alias “Bus Lalith,” following his repatriation from Dubai, where he had been hiding under Interpol Red Notice, with the suspect wanted in connection with multiple cases of murder, attempted murder, drug trafficking, extortion, arson and serious assault.

title: El Niño may bring above-average rainfall, flood risk in October-November
byline: Sri Lanka could experience above-average rainfall during October and November due to prevailing El Niño conditions, raising the possibility of flooding in some areas, the Department of Meteorology has warned.

title: World’s oceans hit highest temperature on record as El Niño grows
byline: The world’s oceans are hotter than ever recorded, new data suggests, as they suffer from human-caused climate change and the growing El Niño weather phenomenon.

title: Chemical release triggers water supply shutdown in Colombo and Gampaha
byline: The temporary suspension of water supply to several areas in the Colombo and Gampaha districts following the release of a chemical into the environment by a private factory has raised serious concerns over the safety of drinking water in the affected areas.

title: US$36bn export dream needs labour reform, not a 1940s engine: TPA’s Barath Arullsamy
byline: Sri Lanka’s ambition to earn US$36 billion from exports by 2030 risks becoming “a glossy brochure resting on a 1940s labour engine” unless the Government urgently introduces a modern Employment Act, Vice President (International Affairs) Democratic Peoples Front - Tamil Progressive Alliance  Barath Arullsamy said.

title: US removes Syria from list of state sponsors of terrorism
byline: The US has removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after 47 years, lifting what it said was the ’’final major barriers’’ for private sector investment in the country and its reintegration into the global economy.

title: Forensic report submitted to court in Ven. Hemaratana Thera case
byline: Government Analyst has reported to the Anuradhapura Magistrate’s Court that the rug, which is a case production in the case against Ven. Pallegama Hemarathana Thera, contained semen of the suspect. However, his report indicated that the strands of hair subject to analysis were not those of the girl who is alleged to have been raped by the suspect and those of another woman. Govt. Analyst further reported that any stains of blood were not visible

title: BASL raises gratification concern over judges’ tenure extension
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL), in a Special Determination petition filed before the Supreme Court challenging the constitutionality of the proposed Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution, has raised concerns over whether the extension of the tenure and related benefits proposed for sitting judges could amount to a “gratification” under the Anti-Corruption Act.

title: Tug-of-war delays cancer treatment equipment for five years
byline: The procurement of advanced cancer radiation treatment machines for Sri Lanka’s public health system has been delayed for nearly five years, putting the lives of thousands of cancer patients at risk, Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights Chairman Specialist Dr Chamal Sanjeewa said.

title: Over 16,600 people affected by adverse weather
byline: A total of 16,647 people from 4,241 families have been affected by adverse weather conditions reported across several districts of Sri Lanka from 6.00 p.m. on August 3 to 6.00 a.m. today (25), to the latest situation report issued by the Disaster Management Centre (DMC) said.

title: QR fuel system to continue amid Middle East tensions
byline: The Government will continue the QR-based fuel distribution system as conflicts in the Middle East remain unresolved, Cabinet Spokesperson Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said today.

title: Billions in Mannar basin oil and gas put up for international exploration
byline: Sri Lanka has opened nearly 34,000 square kilometres of the Mannar Basin to international energy companies for petroleum exploration, raising fresh questions over the country’s potentially vast but largely untapped oil and gas resources.

title: Man held over illegal road construction
byline: A man has been arrested for allegedly entering the Panilkanda Reserve in the Deniyaya area of Matara District without authorization and constructing a road through the forest to gain access to private land.

title: Castlereagh, Maussakelle reservoirs reach overflow levels
byline: Water levels in the Castlereagh and Maussakelle reservoirs have reached overflow levels amid intermittent rainfall in their catchment areas, reservoir engineers said.

title: Training aircraft crashes during landing at Ratmalana Airport
byline: A light training aircraft piloted by a trainee pilot was involved in an accident while landing at Ratmalana Airport today.

title: Court fines Jaffna restaurant Rs. 950,000 for overcharging on bottled water
byline: A popular vegetarian restaurant in the Nallur area of Jaffna has been fined Rs. 950,000 for selling bottled drinking water at an excessive price.

title: New service category for medical, dental specialists
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to appoint an official committee to draft a Service Minute to establish a dedicated service category named the “Specialist Medical Officers and Specialist Dental Surgeons Service” within Sri Lanka’s health sector.

title: Retd. Air Vice Marshal Fernando appointed DMT Chief
byline: The Cabinet has approved the appointment of Air Vice Marshal (Retd.) Thushara Indunil Fernando as the Commissioner General of the Department of Motor Traffic (DMT).

title: Cabinet nod to install 300,000 smart meters across Sri Lanka
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval for a project to install 300,000 smart meters equipped with a Time-of-Use (TOU) billing system, marking a key step in modernizing Sri Lanka’s national electricity grid.

title: 10+ years in media? Applications open for journalist housing units
byline: The Ministry of Health and Mass Media has called for applications from journalists for the “Homagama Journalists’ Housing Scheme,” introduced for media professionals working in print, electronic and online media institutions.

title: Cabinet approves Rs. 104.9 bn central expressway road project
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal to develop connecting roads linking Sections I, III and IV of the Central Expressway with the existing road network in the Western, Central and North-Western provinces.

title: Vedda Chief Vannilattho leaves for India on pilgrimage
byline: Vedda community leader Uruwarige Vannilattho left Sri Lanka today (25) for a pilgrimage to Dambadiva, India, marking his first such journey since assuming leadership of the community.

title: Sugeeshwara Bandara further remanded
byline: The Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court today ordered former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa’s former Private Secretary, Sugeeshwara Lenin Bandara, to be further remanded till September 09 over allegations of criminal misappropriation of funds allocated under the Presidential Expenditure Head.

title: Railway union accuses GM over engine failures
byline: Sri Lanka Railways Station Masters’ Union (SLRSMU) has called for an urgent investigation into the recent breakdowns of locomotive engines, alleging that the current Railway General Manager (GM) should be among those scrutinised over the incidents.

title: Eleven new envoys present credentials to President
byline: Eleven newly appointed Ambassadors and High Commissioners to Sri Lanka presented their credentials to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat today (25).

title: Govt. prepares for El Niño food supply risks
byline: The Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development Ministry has begun preparations to ensure an uninterrupted supply of essential food items and stable prices amid the possible global impact of the El Niño weather phenomenon.

title: 90-day extension obtained to detain Suresh Sallay
byline: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has secured approval to detain retired Major General Suresh Sallay, former head of the State Intelligence Service, for a further 90 days as investigations into the 2019 Easter Sunday terrorist attacks continue.

title: UN and Red Cross warn ’risks have intensified,’ urge regulation of killer robots
byline: The United Nations and the Red Cross warned on Tuesday that the world is ’’dangerously close’’ to a future where autonomous weapons, so-called ’’killer robots,’’ could target humans and issued an urgent appeal for international regulations.

title: Parliament Committee seeks Police Proposals to Ease Prison Overcrowding
byline: The Sectoral Oversight Committee on Governance, Justice and Civil Protection has sought proposals from the Police Department on measures to address overcrowding in Sri Lankan prisons.
